subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — Orion Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@orionhealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — Orion Health

Hi Sam / Procurement team —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of needs (what I heard):
- Reserved/dedicated GPU capacity for production inference (low-latency chat + batch embeddings).
- Data isolation requirements: customer-dedicated pool in a VPC, separation from other tenants, KMS for key management.
- Target SLA: 99.9% uptime, p50 latency <120ms for 512-token requests, p95 <350ms.
- Scale plan: baseline 10 concurrent workers with burst to 30 during peak; predictable throughput for up to ~1.2M tokens/day.
- Compliance asks: SOC 2 evidence and network architecture docs for procurement.

Pain points you described:
- Current vendor variability in latency under load and noisy neighbor interference.
- Procurement/regulatory team needs clear isolation and auditability.
- Need predictable monthly unit costs and a straightforward path to scale.

What Redwood proposes (high level):
- Dedicated capacity offering with reserved GPU pool (customer-dedicated nodes) + VPC peering.
- Autoscaling policy with guaranteed baseline and controlled burst capacity; configurable concurrency per model route.
- SLA offering at the Dedicated tier with monitoring and incident routing.
- Security/compliance bundle: SOC 2 report, KMS integration, and audit logging access for your security team.

Attachments: SOW-draft.docx (initial scope & pricing), redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx (ballpark), and a short capacity plan stub.

Next steps / asks: 
1) Can you confirm the baseline concurrency and the peak concurrency numbers (we used baseline 10 / peak 30 above)?
2) Procurement: are there mandatory contract terms or PO steps we should be aware of?
3) Security: please confirm the contact for SOC 2 review — we’ll send the evidence pack and a short architecture diagram.
4) I’ll have Marissa follow up with a technical capacity plan and GPU recommendations (A100 vs H100 equiv) by EOD tomorrow.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min procurement + security sync on Friday 2027-05-22 @ 10:00 AM PT. Does that work?

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com | (650) 555-0198

Ben —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few quick clarifications from our side: 
- Baseline looks right to me — 10 baseline / 30 peak matches our expected peak for month 1. We may need more headroom by Q4 depending on pilot adoption.
- Procurement: we need to follow our standard PO cadence; I’ll have procurement share the template. Key point: we require liability & data handling terms to be visible up front.
- Security: I’m looping in our security reviewer in procurement, but primary contact is me for now. Please send the SOC 2 and architecture diagram.

Also, can you confirm GPU family you recommend and the expected per-token cost delta between quantized and float deployments?

Sam

Orion Health
sam.cho@orionhealth.com

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T18:30:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated capacity post-call recap — Orion Health

Hi Sam —

Following up with the technical details we discussed. High-level recommendations and constraints below. Attached: orion_capacity_plan.pdf with throughput estimates and GPU sizing.

Recommended GPU family:
- H100-equivalent preferred for chat latency and multi-turn KV cache performance. H100 gives better throughput for long context; A100-equivalent is a lower-cost alternative for mainly embeddings/batch workloads.

Sizing: (based on your baseline = 10 / peak = 30)
- Baseline pool: 4 H100-equivalent GPUs with continuous batching and prefix/KV caching enabled. This should handle ~10 concurrent low-latency chat sessions at ~512 tokens with p50 ~90-110ms.
- Burst policy: reserve additional 3 GPUs for burst to cover up to 30 concurrent sessions with controlled autoscaler ramp (60s scale-up).
- Embeddings batch lane: separate worker pool (2x A100-equivalent) for high-throughput batch embeddings jobs to avoid cross-impact on chat lanes.

Isolation & networking:
- VPC peering + private subnets; customer-dedicated nodes with tenant isolation.
- KMS for key management and optional HSM integration if required.

SLA and monitoring:
- We can offer a 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated with monthly credits for downtime beyond the threshold.
- Per-route latency SLOs with alerting and token-level cost dashboards in Redwood Console.

Compliance artifacts to send: SOC 2 Type II report, architecture diagram, and data retention policy doc. Ben — I attached the capacity plan and a draft SOW excerpt for procurement.

Let me know if you want adjustments (more baseline GPUs for faster p95, or longer autoscale ramp). Happy to join the procurement call.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Engineer, Dedicated Accounts
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
